description: MUDDI, the Model for Underground Data Definition and Integration, is an Open Geospatial Consortium standard for bringing together data about what lies below ground. The OGC standard page read on 2026-09-28 describes Part 1, the Conceptual Model 1.0 (document 23-024), with official model files and encoding schemas, and explains that it defines classes for integrating information on utility networks, transport infrastructure, soils, groundwater and environmental conditions: a mandatory core for built infrastructure networks plus optional classes for the natural and built subsurface. An OGC blog of March 2026 traces the standard to the failure to map underground utilities after the World Trade Center collapse, notes that it builds on the ASCE 38 and 75 standards, the INSPIRE utility specification and the CityGML Utility Network extension, and that it underpins the United Kingdom's National Underground Asset Register. Coverage is not geographic: it is a data model for any city or country. Access is free; no licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: it is a conceptual model, so implementations need an encoding and agreement between utilities on sharing. It supports interdependency and emergency studies, such as merging water, power, telecom and transit tunnels into one subsurface model to trace what a burst main or excavation could hit. Related records: the CityGML Utility Network extension and CityGML.
